_note: One shared definition per term, used by every ⓘ tooltip. Keys are code names and never shown; 'label' is the on-screen name. {placeholders} are filled from accounts.json so numbers always match the pipeline.

account.label: Account
account.text: A customer company, as it appears in Salesforce.

segment.label: Segment
segment.text: Customer size band: Enterprise, Mid-Market or Commercial.

segment_region.label: Region
segment_region.text: Sales region: AMER, EMEA, APAC or LATAM.

rank.label: Rank
rank.text: Position among all {total_accounts} accounts, sorted by opportunity value. #1 is worth the most time.

propensity_score.label: Propensity score
propensity_score.text: 0–100 score for how likely a customer is to grow soon if we invest technical time.

top_reasons.label: Top reasons
top_reasons.text: The three signals that added the most points to the Propensity score, in plain English.

pool_of_funds.label: Pool of funds
pool_of_funds.text: Money available to unlock: unused commit plus open pipeline.

unused_commit.label: Unused commit
unused_commit.text: Spend the customer already committed to but hasn't used yet. Helping them use it protects the renewal.

open_pipeline.label: Open pipeline
open_pipeline.text: Expansion deals currently open in Salesforce for this customer.

expected_value.label: Opportunity value
expected_value.text: Propensity score ÷ 100 × Pool of funds: the money we can realistically help unlock.

ev_covered.label: Opportunity value covered
ev_covered.text: Opportunity value of the accounts that fit within current team capacity.

annual_commit.label: Annual commit
annual_commit.text: What the customer contracted to spend this year.

consumed.label: Used so far
consumed.text: Commit used to date, in dollars.

burn_rate_monthly.label: Monthly spend
burn_rate_monthly.text: Dollars used per month so far (used so far ÷ months elapsed). It says how fast, not whether that's fast enough.

burn_pace.label: On-track %
burn_pace.text: Share of commit used ÷ share of the contract year passed. 100% = exactly on schedule; 90% = slightly behind; below 50% = using it at under half the needed rate.

on_track_status.label: On-track status
on_track_status.text: On track at {on_track_good}+, Slightly behind from {on_track_warn} to just under {on_track_good}, Behind below {on_track_warn}. These bands are assumptions.

expected_consumed_to_date.label: Expected by now
expected_consumed_to_date.text: What a customer spending evenly through the year would have used by today (commit × share of year passed).

behind_pace_amount.label: Behind by
behind_pace_amount.text: Expected by now minus used so far: the dollar gap to being on schedule.

required_monthly_burn.label: Needed monthly spend
required_monthly_burn.text: Monthly spend needed from today to use the full commit by renewal (unused commit ÷ months left).

usage_growth.label: Usage growth
usage_growth.text: Change in product usage over the last {win_usage} days vs. the {win_usage} days before.

new_developers.label: New builders
new_developers.text: Developers who started building on the platform at this customer in the last {win_newdev} days. As an alert: {newdev_min}+ new builders, likely a new team or project.

sa_meetings.label: SA meetings
sa_meetings.text: Meetings with a Solutions Architect in the last {win_eng} days.

days_to_renewal.label: Days to renewal
days_to_renewal.text: Days until the current contract ends. As an alert: renewal is within {renewal_days} days, time to prepare it.

flags.label: Alerts
flags.text: "Why now" signals that call for action this week. Thresholds are assumptions in the decision log.

commit_at_risk.label: Commit at Risk
commit_at_risk.text: At least {car_min_elapsed} into the contract and On-track % below {car_pace}.

usage_spike.label: Usage Spike
usage_spike.text: Last {spike_recent} days ran at {spike}× or more of the {spike_baseline}-day average. Something new probably launched.

quadrant.label: Type of help
quadrant.text: One of four kinds of help, set by Propensity score and Pool of funds: Deep engagement (SA + FDE), Scaled SA programs, Strategic Bet, or Digital / self-serve.

fde_deep_engagement.label: Deep engagement (SA + FDE)
fde_deep_engagement.text: SA leads design and the relationship; FDE builds with the customer's developers until the first production workload.

scaled_sa_program.label: Scaled SA programs
scaled_sa_program.text: SAs only, in group formats: office hours, workshops, reference architectures. No FDE.

strategic_bet.label: Strategic Bet
strategic_bet.text: SA-led discovery with the account team; FDE only if a real project appears.

digital.label: Digital / self-serve
digital.text: No SA/FDE time: docs, templates and alerts.

capacity.label: Team capacity
capacity.text: How many accounts the SA/FDE team can actively cover. Assumed: the top {capacity} by opportunity value.

coverage.label: Coverage
coverage.text: Whether the account is inside the top {capacity} that get dedicated help.

motion.label: Help plan
motion.text: The specific help the account gets, from its type of help and team capacity.

program.label: Program
program.text: Which catch-up program applies: the Commit Burn Sprint, an FDE-led catch-up plan, or the comparison group.

holdout.label: Comparison group
holdout.text: {holdout_share} of Sprint accounts, picked at random and measured but not enrolled, so we can see the program's real impact.

treated.label: Enrolled
treated.text: Sprint accounts that get the program, compared against the comparison group.

impact.label: Impact
impact.text: How much more the enrolled accounts improve than the comparison group.

group.label: Group
group.text: Enrolled accounts get the program; the comparison group is measured only.

goal.label: Goal
goal.text: The one outcome this engagement is working toward.

owner.label: Owner
owner.text: The person accountable for the engagement's next step.

status.label: Status
status.text: On track, At risk or Blocked, judged by the owner each week.

blocker.label: Blocker
blocker.text: What is stopping progress right now, if anything.

next_step.label: Next step
next_step.text: The single next action, ideally with a date.

engagement_health.label: Engagement health
engagement_health.text: Active engagements by status: on track, at risk or blocked.

money_in_play.label: Money in play
money_in_play.text: Total Pool of funds across all accounts: unused commit plus open pipeline.

accounts_count.label: Accounts
accounts_count.text: Number of customer accounts in the group.

tier.label: Tier
tier.text: Package size of the services offer.

scope.label: Scope
scope.text: What the services team delivers in this tier.

indicative_price.label: Price
indicative_price.text: Price per engagement for this tier.

deals_per_year.label: Deals / yr
deals_per_year.text: How many of this tier we assume we'd sell in a year.

services_revenue.label: Services revenue
services_revenue.text: Price × deals per year: revenue from the services themselves.

pull_through.label: Usage pull-through
pull_through.text: Assumed extra yearly platform usage after the migration, often the bigger prize than the services fee.

jd_keyword.label: Role keywords
jd_keyword.text: Phrases from the job description that this part of the prototype demonstrates.

responsibility.label: Responsibility
responsibility.text: A duty listed in the job description.

built.label: What we built
built.text: The part of this prototype that demonstrates that duty.

page.label: Page
page.text: Where to see it on this site.

step.label: Step
step.text: One stage of the lifecycle, from raw data to measured impact.

explanation.label: Simple explanation
explanation.text: What happens at this step, in one plain sentence.

layer.label: Layer
layer.text: Stage of the data, like a warehouse: raw, processed, output, site.

file.label: File
file.text: Where that layer lives in the project folder.

holds.label: What it holds
holds.text: What one row or record in that file contains.
